style: Gilded Lamplight: warm arcane brass clockwork wizard tower (docs/art-bible.md). Brass, walnut, glass and steam. No speech, no music unless the cue is a sting.

cues.text: A knuckle strikes a solid metal service plate. A dry, high tap dies almost immediately.
The same knuckle strike excites the empty chamber behind a metal panel. A low ringing tail and two short reflections follow the tap.
Two dry paper creases open, followed by a softer rustle as the sheet settles in the reader's hands.
A single thick card slid quickly off a walnut deck with a soft paper whisper and a tiny brass clip tick. Dry, close, no reverb, one-shot.
A heavy card thrown fast through the air: short bright whoosh rising then fading, with a faint brass metallic shimmer in the tail. Dry, one-shot.
A thick brass-edged card slapping flat onto a polished walnut tabletop: solid wooden thud with a short metallic ring. Dry, close, one-shot.
Two heavy brass dice tumbling and clattering across a polished walnut table, bouncing several times and slowing down. Metallic clicks and wooden knocks. Dry, one-shot.
A brass die rocking to a stop on a walnut table: two or three fast decaying wobble clicks, then a final small settling tick and silence. Dry, one-shot.
A soft continuous magical hum with a faint crackling shimmer, like a glowing amber finger drawing on glass. Steady, warm, airy, no melody, no pitch movement, seamless loop.
A magical sigil being completed: bright rising shimmer, a warm resonant brass-bell chime burst, then a glittering airy tail fading out. Arcane, golden, one-shot.
A failed spell: a weak crackling spark that sputters, a short descending fizz and a dull little pop. Small, deflating, one-shot.
A brass steam valve releasing a burst of pressurised steam: sharp hiss that peaks fast then decays, with a faint metallic pipe resonance. Dry, one-shot.
A heavy brass gear locking into place with a single solid metallic clank, a short ratchet click before it and a brief ring after. Dry, one-shot.
A heavy oak door with iron hinges and a brass clockwork latch: latch clicks, the door groans open slowly with a low creak and a soft thump at the end. One-shot.
A tiny crisp brass mechanical tick, like a clockwork escapement click. Very short, dry, quiet, one-shot interface sound.
A heavy blow on a brass automaton: dull metallic clang with a rattle of loose gears and a short ringing decay. Dry, one-shot.
A brass clockwork automaton breaking down: a burst of grinding gears, a spring snapping, a falling cascade of metal parts clattering, a final winding-down whir and a last clink. One-shot.
A folding walnut table with brass hinges opening out: smooth wooden creak, hinge clicks, latches snapping into place, ending with a solid soft thump. One-shot.
A warm bright reward chime: three quick ascending notes on a small brass music-box and glockenspiel, golden shimmer tail. Pleasant, short, one-shot.
One quiet, dry grandfather-clock escapement tick. Brief wood contact and a small brass click, with a fast natural decay.
Original deterministic clockwork bell strike, low note. One short dry brass strike with a fundamental and two decaying metallic partials, no melody, no reverb.
Original deterministic clockwork bell strike, middle note. One short dry brass strike with a fundamental and two decaying metallic partials, no melody, no reverb.
Original deterministic clockwork bell strike, high note. One short dry brass strike with a fundamental and two decaying metallic partials, no melody, no reverb.
A somber defeat sting: low brass drone and a slow descending minor chime phrase, a clockwork mechanism winding down to a stop, then quiet. One-shot.
A triumphant victory sting: a short rising fanfare of warm brass and bells resolving to a bright major chord with a golden shimmering tail. One-shot.
A small brass coin or cog picked up: a bright quick metallic jingle of two tiny clinks. Short, light, dry, one-shot.
A protective ward raising: a resonant metallic shield-up chime with a short airy swell and a solid ringing brass tone fading out. One-shot.
A pressure gate opening: a sharp steam hiss, a metal lock releasing, and a heavy iron clank as the gate settles. Dry, one-shot.
A counterweight grille opening: a short chain and ratchet climb, followed by an iron grille sliding along its track and settling heavily. Dry, one-shot.
A thin service panel opening: a small metal latch snaps, the light panel swings on its hinge, and its edge taps the frame. Dry, one-shot.
A thorn ward opening: dry fibers and brittle leaves release in a close papery rasp, with a few small twig snaps as the growth retracts. Dry, one-shot.
An archive ink door opening: sapphire resonance blooms through old masonry, then a low stone-and-metal latch drops into place. Dry, one-shot.
An archive stillwind door opening: a descending fan winds down through a hollow shaft, ending with a broad metal grille sliding and thudding home. Dry, one-shot.
An archive mirror door opening: glass resonates with a clear crystalline ring while a hinged metal frame swings free and settles against its stop. Dry, one-shot.
An astral lift opening: a pair of heavy sliding metal doors part together with a deep rail rumble, then meet their stops with a matched double clank. Dry, one-shot.
Three quick glass contacts, a clean metal guide slide, and a light mechanical stop as the prism gate opens.
A pneumatic dispatch room opening: a short hollow capsule clatter and tick, followed by an air piston release, a ribbed iron shutter sliding, and two lugs seating. Dry, one-shot.
Speaking Pipes send: one dry lever clack, then a short breath of air drawn into the pipe. Broad inharmonic contact and filtered air only, no pitched tone, no melody, no reverb. One-shot.
Cistern grille opening: a brief damp pipe echo in wet masonry, a heavy cast-iron catch, rough grille rubbing along stone, then the grille settles into its stop. One-shot, no speech, no music.

Stone reliquary opening: a short dry brass bolt release at 0.04 seconds, heavy granular stone movement from 0.18 to 1.2 seconds, then a settled low stone thump at 1.25 seconds with a clean short tail. No water, steam, wood, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic optical receiver proof: two bright glass resonances arrive as a clean two-note interval, then resolve into a dry brass snap with a soft sustained optical tail. Positional mono, close and dry, one-shot, no speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic Borrowed Light stone recess opening: a counterweighted stone leaf slides across grit, three metallic ratchet teeth mark the travel, and a final low stone footfall seats the leaf. Positional mono, close and dry, one-shot, distinct from a pressure gate, no steam, wood, speech, music, or reverb.
A quietly burning wooden torch with scattered small resin ticks and a continuous ember bed.
Iron links drag under tension as the Lantern Bailiff winds its chain. A short ratchet catch marks the end of the pull.
The Mortar Scarab rasps across stone, followed by three quick metallic leg contacts and a short stone settle.

Original deterministic dry close steam leak loop for the Valvehouse: a restrained continuous pressurised hiss with subtle breath modulation, no voice, music, pitch movement, room reverb, or sharp transients. Seamless 9-second loop.

Original deterministic Valvehouse gate opening one-shot: dry steam pressure rush begins immediately, followed by clearly distinctive iron rail motion, then a solid metal clank at 1.12 seconds when the gate reaches the top. No voice, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic one-shot for the Pendulum Gallery: two aligned pendulums make a clean brass synchronization catch in the first 0.06 seconds, two relatively light bronze hinge movements open antique double doors from 0.16 to 1.0 seconds, and a soft pair of bronze stop contacts lands around 1.08 to 1.15 seconds. Dry, close, short tail, no steam, stone, rail grille, generic wood creak, speech, music, or reverb.
A clockwork ratchet winds up, then two steel armor plates seat as the armory mannequin awakens.

Original deterministic glass-chamber reservoir fill: a focused bubbling brass inlet pipe and small water bubbles rise in pitch and intensity over 0.65 seconds. Close, dry, mono positional one-shot, no melody, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic glass-chamber reservoir drain: a thin outlet produces falling liquid gurgles and a brief hollow suction at the end over 0.65 seconds. Close, dry, mono positional one-shot, no melody, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic glass-chamber release: a quick brass fitting snap, then a short stone shutter scraping aside and settling firmly on its stop over 0.85 seconds. Close, dry, mono positional one-shot, no speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic Shadow Stencil slide: a thin brass rail carries a pierced shutter a short distance with a fine guide scrape, three restrained travel ticks, and one precise brass detent click at the end. Close, dry, mono positional one-shot, no stone, steam, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic Shadow Stencil release: a heavy stone floor tile depresses with a low compact thud, a brass latch snaps free, then a short narrow drawer scrape ends in a firm stop. Close, dry, mono positional one-shot, distinct from the reservoir shutter, with no water, steam, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic positional spring workshop cue: a short taut iron spring winds under a key, with three crisp pawl teeth and a tiny dry metal settle. Close, dry, mono one-shot, no melody, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic positional spring workshop cue: a mechanism lifts halfway against tension, catches with two restrained iron clicks, then falls back into a dull low seat. Close, dry, mono one-shot, no stone grille, steam, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic positional spring workshop cue: a wound spring releases quickly into a bright descending click-and-chatter cascade, ending with a compact iron body settle. Close, dry, mono one-shot, no melody, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic positional spring workshop cue: the spring disengages, an iron portcullis lifts with heavy guided rail motion, then a deep latch seats firmly. Distinct from the earlier stone grille mechanism, close and dry, mono one-shot, no steam, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic Dark Circuit bridge contact: a short clipped brass contact tick with a small contained electrical snap, signaling a reversible seated or lifted bridge. Close, dry, mono positional one-shot, no hum, melody, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic Dark Circuit grille opening: a distinct solenoid clack, ascending toothed rack clicks under a rolling lift, and a final metallic lock stop. Close, dry, mono positional one-shot, no wooden door, steam, speech, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic Drum Gallery low reed stab: one dry mechanical musical-reed strike with a low brass body, a compact inharmonic bite, and a short decay. Distinct single note, not a melody, close mono positional one-shot, no reverb.

Original deterministic Drum Gallery middle reed stab: one dry mechanical musical-reed strike with a focused brass body, a compact inharmonic bite, and a short decay. Distinct single note, not a melody, close mono positional one-shot, no reverb.

Original deterministic Drum Gallery high reed stab: one dry mechanical musical-reed strike with a bright brass body, a compact inharmonic bite, and a short decay. Distinct single note, not a melody, close mono positional one-shot, no reverb.

Original deterministic Drum Gallery index tick: a quiet dry wood-and-brass step tick used on every beat, including silence. Very short, restrained, close mono positional one-shot, no pitch phrase, music, or reverb.
Original deterministic Drum Gallery pin seat and lift: a short metal pin contact, a compact springy brass seat, and a smaller lift-off tick. Dry close mono positional one-shot, no music or reverb.

Original deterministic Drum Gallery grille lift: a unique low ratchet-drum undertone, five dry ascending rack teeth, then two separated latch and chunk contacts as the compact gate lifts. Close mono positional one-shot, no melody, steam, voice, or reverb.

Original deterministic Trellis Keeper brace tell: two short taut ratchet contacts pull into a restrained metallic leaf and hinge knock. Dry close mono positional one-shot, no wooden door, voice, music, or reverb.

Original deterministic Trellis Keeper double-cut: two mechanically distinct dry metal shear clacks in quick succession, first bright and clipped, second lower and heavier. Audible as two separate contacts on the enemy action, no wooden door, voice, music, or reverb.
